detailed_description: Merge Conflict Resolver helps clean up Git conflict markers in pasted text. It recognizes standard <<<<<<<, =======, and >>>>>>> blocks, then applies one choice to every conflict in the input: keep the current branch, keep the incoming branch, or keep both chunks in order. The resolved output can be copied back to your editor. The page is a marker cleaner, not a semantic code merge engine, so review the merged result before committing.
usage_steps: Paste file content that contains Git conflict markers.
Choose Use current, Use incoming, or Keep both.
Copy the result back into your editor.
Run your formatter, tests, and normal Git checks before committing.
usage_examples: Remove conflict markers from a small README conflict after choosing the incoming text.
Keep both chunks from a changelog conflict and edit the final order manually.
Resolve a simple package or config conflict before running project validation.
Check how a current-branch-only resolution would look without editing the original file.

faqs.question: Does this merge code intelligently?
faqs.answer: No. It only removes standard Git conflict marker blocks according to the selected mode.

faqs.question: Can I choose separately for each conflict?
faqs.answer: No. The selected mode applies to every conflict block in the pasted text.

faqs.question: What happens if the conflict markers are incomplete?
faqs.answer: The tool keeps the original text instead of producing a destructive partial output.

faqs.question: Should I commit the output immediately?
faqs.answer: No. Always review the result, format the file, and run the relevant tests or build before committing.
